title: Strict sign representation
statement: Let $X$ be a type, let $f$ assign to each $x\in X$ a sign in $\{-1,1\}$, and let $p:X\to\mathbb{R}$. Suppose that for every $x\in X$, the value of the sign $f(x)$ multiplied by $p(x)$ is strictly positive. Then for every $x\in X$, $f(x)=1$ when $p(x)\geq 0$ and $f(x)=-1$ when $p(x)<0$, and $p(x)\neq 0$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $x\in X$, the real value of $f(x)$ times $p(x)$ is strictly positive
